Voat Plays Final Fantasy I

Initially released in Japan in 1987, the original FINAL FANTASY amazed audiences with its rich story and stunning graphics.

Players guide the Warriors of Light as they set out on a quest to restore the crystals to their former luster. Its side view battles, choice and promotion of character classes, and sprawling world explored with fantastic vehicles quickly became standards of the series. This game set the stage for all FINAL FANTASY games to come.

About 8 years ago, I worked for a company that relied on Cisco networking equipment. It was my responsibilty to write software to communicate with them for configuration purposes, monitoring purposes, &c.

It was hilarious how many bugs I ran into. For example, let's say you want to know how much traffic was going through a particular switch. Well, the switches have internal counters. Every time a byte goes over the network interface, it is supposed to increase that counter by one. Then you can ask the switch what number the counter currently reads. Dead simple, right? Wrong. That counter could go down for no reason.

Our network guy complained to me that my software wasn't working right. I showed him the raw logs of what I was seeing. He does some testing himself. Ends up having to notify Cisco of he problem and wait months for a patch. The counter is only supposed to go up - there is no conceivable instance when it should go down - once a byte is sent out of the network, there is conceptuallno way to undo that! It already happened!

Another time, our network admins were configuring some new equipment because they need to do some more complex routing with our network. They do everything right. Then the double check it. Then they make it live. Massive disaster when a previously "undocumented" feature is activated by the configuration. The BGP tables are fucked and all of our peers hate us.

After much research, Cisco is able to explain what happened and issues a patch.

TL;DR Cisco's equipment is critical to the functioning of the internet, but I've seen them fuck up so bad that they can't even count properly....

(For those of you who know your shit and try to call me out, yes, I realize how the counters "flip over" and reset to zero when they hit their limits. Obviously a 64-bit counter can't go up forever. The problem was that it was sometimes counting down. Hrm... why would you want something that measures traffic and should only go up, go down? Well, that's one way I can think of to hide traffic that people don't want seen. After all, which network admins are going to tap the physical line to make sure everything is adding up. This wasn't used equipment found on eBay; this was from the company directly. We needed that equipment and paid for it.)
